correctness.rationale: The verifier constructs both the facet-downward closure and the independent complement-connectivity predicate over all 4096 subsets and proves their complete agreement. Both opposite-order acyclic matchings are checked against all 13224 covering incidences. Every exact integer cancellation has a checked unit pivot and chain square zero. The two resulting Smith forms independently give Z/2 in degree 4 and free rank 30 in degree 6; direct unreduced mod-two boundary ranks agree with universal-coefficient predictions. The shellability and wedge consequences follow from standard torsion-freeness properties. The computations are finite and executable, not extrapolations.

value.rationale: The canonical icosahedral graph is a natural planar vertex-transitive object, and its ordinary five-cut complex is a direct extension of a motivated topology-of-cut-complexes program. The first observed nonzero integral torsion gives a meaningful obstruction to two structural properties, shellability and homotopy equivalence to a sphere wedge, in contrast to the previously published artificial torsion construction. The exact entire integral homology is a reusable finite invariant; no generalization is improperly claimed.
